title: Upstream/Downstream with Variable Currents
tagline: Year 3 — Stream speed that changes, boats that turn back, drifting objects and average speed in streams

introduction.overview: Year 2 boats and streams used a constant stream speed and a single trip. Year 3 adds streams whose speed differs in different stretches, boats that turn back after some time, objects that simply drift with the current, and round trips where the average speed is requested. The tools are the same: downstream speed = b + s, upstream speed = b − s, and relative speed between the boat and a drifting object is the boat's speed in still water.
introduction.placementRelevance: Advanced boats-and-streams questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds, typically with a turn-back or a drifting object.
introduction.realWorldContext: Ferries crossing tidal rivers, rescue boats chasing floating objects and river cruises with different current zones follow these rules.

learningObjectives: Handle journeys across stretches with different stream speeds
Solve turn-back problems and the meeting point of boat and drifting object
Use the fact that a drifting object moves at the stream speed
Compute the average speed of a round trip
Find b and s from time data in two directions

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Downstream = b + s. Upstream = b − s. Boat speed in still water b = (downstream + upstream)/2; stream s = (downstream − upstream)/2.

coreDefinitions: Drifting object: an object with no engine; it moves at the stream speed.
Turn-back problem: a boat travels for some time, turns and returns to a point.
Variable current: different stream speeds in different stretches.
Round-trip average speed: total distance ÷ total time.
Relative speed of boat and drifting object: the boat's speed in still water, whichever way the boat goes.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Seen from the water, the stream disappears: the boat just moves at its own speed b relative to the water, and a drifting object does not move at all. Many puzzles become simple when you work in the frame of the water.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For time questions, work in the water frame: the distance between boat and drifting object changes at b per hour, whatever the stream does. For round trips compute each leg separately using the leg's own stream speed.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Effective speeds
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Downstream b + s;  upstream b − s

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Water frame
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Relative speed of boat and drifting object = b
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: Boat turns after t hours; meets object after another t hours

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Two-direction data
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: 24 km down in 2 h, up in 3 h → b 10, s 2

mainNarrative: For a stretch-by-stretch journey, compute each stretch with its own stream speed. A boat with b = 10 km/h crosses 12 km of water flowing at 2 km/h downstream (12 km/h, 1 h) and then 12 km at 4 km/h upstream (6 km/h, 2 h): total 24 km in 3 h, an average speed of 8 km/h.
Round trip average: for equal distances at downstream speed u and upstream speed v, the average is 2uv/(u + v). With u = 12 and v = 8, it is 192/20 = 9.6 km/h, less than the boat's speed 10 km/h.

Drifting objects move at the stream speed s. A boat passes a floating log and goes on for t hours upstream, then turns back; in the water frame the boat moves away from the log at speed b for t hours and returns at b for t hours, so it meets the log again after 2t hours of boat time, wherever the stream is.

To find b and s from timings for the same distance D, use b = (D/t₁ + D/t₂)/2 and s = (D/t₁ − D/t₂)/2 with t₁ downstream and t₂ upstream: 24 km in 2 h downstream and 3 h upstream gives 12 and 8, so b = 10 and s = 2.
A man rows downstream for a time and upstream for the same time; his net displacement is (b + s)t − (b − s)t = 2st downstream, a useful shortcut for turn-back problems.

deepDiveAspects.title: Drifting object shortcut
deepDiveAspects.content: If a boat goes upstream for t hours from a drifting object and then returns, it meets the object after 2t hours (regardless of the stream), because both frames share the same current.

deepDiveAspects.title: Stream faster than boat
deepDiveAspects.content: If s ≥ b, the boat cannot go upstream. Questions will always keep b > s.

solvedExamples.title: Boat speed and stream from timings
solvedExamples.question: A boat takes 2 hours to go 24 km downstream and 3 hours to return. Find the boat's speed in still water and the stream speed.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The boat's speed is the mean of the two effective speeds.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Using the average speed 9.6 as b.

solvedExamples.title: Floating object
solvedExamples.question: A boat (speed 8 km/h in still water) passes a floating log and travels 2 hours upstream, then turns back. How long after turning does it meet the log again?

steps.title: In the water frame
steps.explanation: Boat moves away from the log at 8 km/h for 2 h: 16 km.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The stream speed does not matter.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Computing with a stream speed that is not given.

solvedExamples.title: Average speed of a round trip
solvedExamples.question: A boat goes 12 km/h downstream and 8 km/h upstream. What is its average speed for a round trip of equal distances?

shortcutMethods.title: Water frame

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Track each object in the ground frame.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Remove the stream: relative to water the boat moves at b and a drifting object is at rest. Use ground speeds only for distances.

rulesForApplication: Equal times each way: net 2st downstream.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using ground speed in the water frame

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Round-trip average speed must be less than b.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Draw both frames when a drifting object appears.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Many puzzles reduce to "the stream does not matter".

easy.question: A boat takes 2 hours to go 24 km downstream and 3 hours to return. Its speed in still water is (km/h)
For the same boat, the stream speed is (km/h)
The downstream and upstream speeds are 12 and 8 km/h. The average speed for a round trip is (km/h)

intermediate.question: A boat (b = 10 km/h) crosses 12 km with a downstream current of 2 km/h and then 12 km with an upstream current of 4 km/h. The total time is (hours)
intermediate.explanation: First stretch 12/12 = 1 h. Second stretch at 10 − 4 = 6 km/h takes 2 h. Total 3 h.

intermediate.question: For the previous journey (24 km in 3 hours), the average speed is (km/h)
A boat passes a floating log, goes 2 hours upstream and then turns back. It meets the log after turning back in (hours)
intermediate.explanation: In the water frame the boat returns at the same speed it left: 2 hours.

advanced.question: A boat (b = 12 km/h) goes downstream with a stream of 3 km/h for 30 minutes and then turns back. The time it takes to return to its starting point is (minutes)
advanced.explanation: Distance = 15 × 0.5 = 7.5 km. Upstream speed = 9 km/h. Time = 7.5/9 h = 50 minutes.

advanced.question: A boat goes 20 km downstream in 2 hours and 20 km upstream in 5 hours. Its speed in still water is (km/h)

placementStyle.question: A person rows to a place and back in 7 hours. He can row 4 km downstream in the time he rows 3 km upstream. If the stream is 1 km/h, the distance to the place is (km)
placementStyle.explanation: Downstream : upstream = 4 : 3 means (b + 1) : (b − 1) = 4 : 3, so b = 7: speeds 8 and 6. D/8 + D/6 = 7 gives 7D/24 = 7, so D = 24.

placementStyle.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h. It goes 30 km upstream and returns in 4 hours 30 minutes. The stream speed is (km/h)
A boat goes downstream at 15 km/h and upstream at 9 km/h. It takes 8 hours to go to a place and return. The distance is (km)
